name: Hasupha
overview: Hasupha was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant, as recorded in Ezra 2:43. His role as a temple servant highlights his involvement in the religious duties associated with the worship of God during the post-exilic period. Beyond this, no additional personal details or notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Hasupha appears once in Scripture without a given meaning or special title. It is simply recorded as a proper name in Ezra 2:43, with no indication that it was given directly by God or carries a particular theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Hasupha is identified as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe responsible for temple service. Scripture does not provide further family relationships or genealogical details beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Hasupha's significance lies in his role as a temple servant among the Levites during the return from exile, emphasizing the restoration of proper worship and religious order in Israel. His mention in Ezra 2:43 situates him within the community that renewed dedication to God’s house, reflecting the ongoing faithfulness of the Levites in their God-ordained duties. Though not a prominent figure, his inclusion underscores the importance of every individual contributing to the spiritual rebuilding of Israel.
